newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: THAI STOCKS SALES RUMOURS HIT SINGAPORE RUBBER.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS SALES RUMOURS HIT SINGAPORE RUBBER.

text.p: Rumours the Thai government is close to selling an estimated 74,000 tonnes of rubber stocks swirled in the Singapore rubber market, dealers said on Friday.

"I heard of the talk the Thais were selling their rubber. That's going to hit prices next week if it is true. All the producers and traders were talking about it," a dealer said. The rumour followed closely on the announcement by a Thai industry official at a trade meeting last week that Thailand's rubber stocks total about 140,000 tonnes.
"We've heard about that. This is going to make people nervous," another trader said.
In other developments, dealers said local shortcovering for RSS3 and TSR20 rubber was seen in the market on Friday with most of the major buyers sitting on the sidelines.

"All the three majors - Bridgestone, Michelin and Goodyear - were out. They called a day off," a dealer said. Another trader said: "Michelin did not buy today. It's a bit quiet out there." At the close of trade, October RSS3 was seen at 96.50 U.S. cents a kg from 96.25 cents. September RSS1 was indicated at 138.25 Singapore cents (94 U.S. cents) a kg from 137.75 cents.
